name: Cybercore

card.summary: A retrofuturistic dressing aesthetic built on late-1990s and early-2000s tech style, using chrome, reflective and synthetic fabrics and futuristic accessories to give a distinctive, cohesive look.
card.note: A style choice; fit and fabric affect how it reads.

quick.overview:
Cybercore is the original meaning of the Y2K internet aesthetic: a retrofuturistic style drawn from products, fashion and graphics of the late 1990s and early 2000s. For someone working on their look, it offers a coherent, recognisable way to dress.

Its clothing vocabulary includes reflective and PVC-style synthetic materials, tracksuits, futuristic sunglasses, platform shoes and wearable technology, in colours such as lime, orange and hot pink set against white and chrome. No research has examined it as a way to improve attractiveness.
quick.how: Practitioners build outfits around metallic and glossy materials, bright accents on a white or chrome base, sleek sunglasses and tech-inspired accessories, sometimes paired with period devices such as flip phones or early digital cameras.
quick.risks: There are no health risks specific to the style. Synthetic and reflective fabrics can be less breathable, and the look is distinctive enough that it reads differently in different settings.

lead: Cybercore is the term now used for the original sense of the Y2K aesthetic: a retrofuturistic internet-era style drawn from late-1990s and early-2000s products, fashion and design. As "Y2K" has broadened to mean 2000s fashion generally, "Cybercore" refers to the earlier, narrower tech-driven look [1].

In clothing, the style uses synthetic materials such as PVC, reflective fabrics, tracksuits, platform shoes, futuristic sunglasses and wearable technology [1][2]. Colours include lime, orange and hot pink alongside white and chrome, and graphics use gradients, glossy effects and rounded fonts [1]. For appearance, it works as a stylemeta: a defined set of garments and accessories that make an outfit look intentional and consistent.

The aesthetic draws on 1970s design, sci-fi imagery and 1990s styles, and is popular in East Asia, including K-pop and J-pop fashion, Japan's "Y3K" trend and 1990s Harajuku cyber fashion [1]. Its 2020s resurgence has been linked to the COVID-19 pandemic and the recession that followed [1].

chain: Pick a cohesive set of reflective, glossy, tech-inspired pieces
Outfit reads as deliberate and distinctive
angle.text: Cybercore gives people a clear dressing template with defined colours, materials and accessories. How well it flatters depends on fit and the wearer.

paras: Wikipedia places the aesthetic after the Memphis Design movement and before Frutiger Aero, and notes the name Y2K comes from programmer David Eddy's abbreviation for the year-2000 computer problem [1]. It describes the look as using metallic or chrome surfaces, blobject forms like Apple's iMac G3, translucent casings and glitter [1].

Wardrobe elements include PVC and other synthetic fabrics, reflective clothing, tracksuits, platform shoes, futuristic sunglasses and wearable technology [1][2]. Period electronics such as flip phones and digital cameras also feature as props and decor [1].

The style is linked to 1970s design trends, 1990s animal prints and psychedelic patterns, and sci-fi imagery, and it has strong roots in East Asian fashion [1]. The article points to the Designers Republic and the Y2K Aesthetic Institute of the Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute as related reference points [1].

timeline.event: Period of products and styles the aesthetic references [1].
Resurgence, linked by Wikipedia to the COVID-19 pandemic and its recession [1].
